# ADR 0139: Authoritative Editor Working Copies and Explicit Persistence

Status: Proposed
Date: 2026-08-17
Amends: ADR 0019
Relates to: ADR 0005, ADR 0007, ADR 0085, ADR 0104, ADR 0121, ADR 0132

## Problem

The Editor has several in-memory authoring models, but their visibility to other subsystems is not uniformly defined.

Scene, Graph, and UI documents live in the active Editor session and carry dirty state. Animation Set has a dedicated editor state with its own in-memory document, undo stack, clean baseline, and explicit save. Other systems may still resolve the same asset from disk. This permits a contradiction:

```text
Animation Set Editor working copy: all Motion Slots are bound
disk copy: older, missing a binding
Scene View / validation / another editor: reads disk
=> Animation Controller appears invalid even though the visible Set is configured
```

Requiring users to press each specialized editor's Save button before Scene View, Inspector, validation, preview, or runtime-debug preparation can observe an edit makes persistence timing part of semantic correctness.

Conversely, writing every keystroke or intermediate invalid edit to disk would create Git churn, complicate Undo/Redo, and make temporary authoring states persist unexpectedly.

The Editor therefore needs one project-wide distinction between authoritative live working copies and persisted saved copies.

## Decision

### 1. An open Editor document has one authoritative working copy

For every authoring document type that participates in the live Editor, there is at most one authoritative working copy for a given stable document/asset identity within the project Editor process.

The working copy is the semantic source of truth for Editor consumers while it is open/registered. It contains the latest accepted Editor transaction whether or not that transaction has been persisted to disk.

Examples include:

- Scene;
- semantic Graph and GraphView;
- Animation Set;
- Material;
- Project Settings where represented as an editable document;
- future Timeline, VFX, UI, or other typed authoring documents.

A specialized editor may own presentation and local selection state, but it MUST NOT own a second semantically independent copy invisible to the rest of the Editor.

### 2. Editor consumers resolve through the working-copy service first

Inspector, Scene View conversion, Problems validation, authoring preview, Graph Debug source resolution, dependency validation, asset inspectors, MCP live authoring, and other Editor-integrated consumers resolve authoring documents through the authoritative working-copy/document registry.

Resolution is conceptually:

```text
request document by stable identity
  -> authoritative open working copy, if present
  -> otherwise load canonical saved copy through normal asset/document service
```

A subsystem MUST NOT bypass an existing working copy by reopening the same document directly from disk for semantic evaluation merely because file I/O is convenient.

Disk remains authoritative for unopened documents and for external tools that are not attached to the live Editor session.

### 3. Working-copy visibility is immediate; disk persistence is explicit

A successful authoring edit updates the authoritative working copy immediately and marks it dirty.

All Editor consumers that observe that document on the next consistent refresh/revision see the same working-copy revision. No dedicated per-window Save operation is required for another Editor subsystem to observe the edit.

Persistence remains explicit:

- `Ctrl+S` saves the active/appropriate dirty document;
- `Save All` persists all dirty registered documents when provided by the Editor;
- specialized Save buttons may remain as aliases to the same persistence service when useful, but they do not gate working-copy visibility;
- disk autosave on every edit is not required and is not the default.

The saved copy is a checkpoint of the working copy, not a competing live source.

### 4. Working copies participate in revision, generation, and transaction contracts

Each authoritative working copy exposes the revision/generation semantics required by its existing authoring service.

Human Editor mutations, live Editor-attached MCP mutations, Undo/Redo, and specialized document tools operate against the same semantic state. Stale revision checks therefore compare against the current working copy, not an independently reloaded file.

This preserves ADR 0121's live Editor authority and avoids a second MCP/file writer.

Undo/Redo changes the working copy immediately and marks dirty/clean according to whether the resulting semantic document equals the saved baseline. Undo does not need to rewrite disk.

### 5. Temporary invalid states do not justify falling back to stale disk

Some UIs may permit a temporary incomplete edit while a control has focus. Such draft widget state is presentation-local and is not yet the authoritative document.

Once an edit is committed into the authoring working copy, consumers observe that exact revision even if domain validation reports errors. They MUST NOT silently substitute the last valid disk copy.

This produces a consistent contract:

- presentation-local draft may be temporarily incomplete;
- committed working-copy revision may be valid or invalid according to domain rules;
- validation reports the actual current revision;
- persistence policy decides whether an invalid revision is serializable/savable;
- no subsystem masks the error with older saved data.

Domains that require mutations to preserve structural validity continue to reject invalid transactions at their existing semantic boundary.
